article_title: The Price of Finding a Certificate: Unsupported Pareto Points under Prefix Queries
article_abstract: We study the cost of discovering a certificate for a designated candidate whose two objectives are means of ordered vector records. Each query purchases the next whole record of one configuration. Algorithms must decide correctly on every legal archive, and their acquisition cost on positive archives is compared with the cheapest realised prefix proving both Pareto nondomination and unsupportedness under nonzero nonnegative weights. This is a geometric instance-complexity problem with mandatory predecessor payments. When the cost coordinate is unbounded, we determine the exact deterministic and zero-error randomised ratios for every catalogue size and archive length. The randomised lower bound covers numerical policies and arbitrary prefix interleavings through a causal Ramsey reduction. Bounded diagonal bands change the feasible certificate structure and yield sharp three-configuration transitions under positive row prices. A fixed three-symbol alphabet retains asymptotic acquisition overhead. On the triangle, a uniform policy has ratio at most 873/800, while approaching the unrestricted lower bound 23/22 requires leaving the candidate partly unread on the exhibited hard family. This separates the search for witnesses from the decision to complete the candidate. A certificate-preservation criterion identifies which domain changes retain positive-input acquisition behaviour. The unrestricted triangle optimum remains open.
